title: Overnight resiliency scrub and runbook deltas
content:
Context: overnight shift (02:00-10:00 PT) scrub focusing on two recurring surface issues: sudden tail-latency spikes in hosted-api and intermittent lowered KV cache hit-rate affecting small-model routes. This doc captures the sequence, mitigations we exercised, observed data, and concrete runbook changes we should make before the next night shift.

Timeline (local PT):
- 02:18 — First elevated p50->p95 divergence on hosted-api chat endpoints (eu-west region). Alert: latency_tail_high_v2 firing.
- 02:22 — Correlated spike with drop in internal kv-cache hit-rate for prefix cache (cache.hit_rate dropped from ~0.92 to ~0.45).
- 02:27 — Initial mitigation: throttled long-running background eval jobs (tag: eval-runner) that were backfilling embeddings; small immediate decrease in incoming cache churn but no full recovery.
- 02:35 — Deployed temporary routing rule to prefer warm model variants (model: redwood-small-v2-warm) for chat routes under 128 tokens while autoscaling started for larger pools.
- 02:44 — p95 reduced to acceptable range but we observed higher error rate for some bursty customers (5xx ~0.8% -> 2.5%).
- 03:10 — Autoscaler stabilized additional workers; cache hit-rate recovered to ~0.88; normal service restored.
- 03:30 — Post-incident sync with infra: discovered a mis-tuned eviction policy in the kv layer that combined with short-lived eval-key prefixes caused thrash.

Observations / Notes to self:
- The spike pattern recurs when embedding backfills or heavy eval traffic concurrently run in the same PGPU pools as hosted traffic. We need clearer isolation (per-minute quotas or scheduling windows).
- Our current cache eviction default is: lru_size=2e6, ttl=10m. During load with many ephemeral keys TTL churn causes lru thrash; consider introducing per-key-type buckets.
- On-call handoff call at 04:00 — Ravi flagged an open question: why routing fallback to warm variant increased 5xx for certain customers. Probably due to model-compatibility mismatch for function-calling code paths; need test harness.

Immediate follow-ups (actionable, owners, rough ETA):
- SRE-3124 (owner: Ravi Patel) — Short-term: add a per-queue throttle for embeddings/backfill jobs during peak traffic windows (ETA: 48h, next steps: propose throttle thresholds in PR).
- SRE-3125 (owner: Lina Cho) — Medium-term: add a second-level bucketed eviction policy to kv-cache (per-prefix namespace buckets) and a simulation to estimate hit-rate under backfill patterns (ETA: 2 weeks).
- SRE-3126 (owner: Marcus Nguyen) — Test-suite: add integration tests that validate routing fallback doesn't change API surface for function-calling (create test harness linking to redwood-small-v2-warm) (ETA: 1 week).
- DOC-OPS-88 (owner: Ava Martinez) — Update Oncall Runbook section: "kv-cache emergency throttle" with exact commands, metrics to watch (cache.hit_rate, cache.evictions_per_min, hosted-api.p95), rollback steps. Put draft in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-4552) (ETA: 24h).

Runbook draft (quick procedural stub — needs formatting and exact command snippets):
1) Detect: alert latency_tail_high_v2 + cache.hit_rate < 0.6 sustained for >3m.
2) Quick mitigation (1st responder): scale down non-user-facing background jobs (eval-runner queue) — command: TODO (ops/playbook trigger).
3) If p95 > target after 5m, enable routing preference to warm variants for routes <128 tokens: route-override set route=chat.* model=redwood-small-v2-warm (note: monitor errors).
4) If 5xx increases >1% after warm fallback, revert routing preference and escalate to infra on-call — suspect model compatibility.
5) If cache.hit_rate not improving in 10m, enable emergency cache-throttle: set kv_cache.max_inserts_per_min=500 for ephemeral-prefixes.
6) Post incident: collect heapshots and eviction logs and tag runbook ticket.

Runbook gaps (explicit):
- Missing CLI command snippets for scaling background jobs (placeholder in this draft).
- No automated test that simulates ephemeral-prefix churn.
- No runbook step linking to an authoritative list of "ephemeral-prefix" name patterns — that mapping lives in a config repo but not documented for oncall.

Open questions (for infra/product sync):
- Can product introduce a sandbox scheduling window for eval/backfills (low-risk low-latency windows), or do we enforce SRE throttles?
- What SLA trade-offs are acceptable for warm-variant fallback? Product wants consistent latency; some customers rely on specific function-calling behavior.

Customer impact notes:
- Affected customers: two small SaaS customers in EU (IDs: cust-1187, cust-2262) reported degraded conversational responsiveness and increased 5xx rates between 02:20-03:05. We should surface this to CSM with a concise summary.

Handoff items for daytime SREs:
- Lina: start simulation runs for bucketed eviction; attach results to SRE-3125.
- Marcus: add test coverage for fallback compatibility; leave notes in PR referenced above.
- Ravi: draft throttle thresholds and put preliminary config in a feature-flagged PR.
- Ava: finish runbook doc and link Confluence id in SRE ticket.

Misc notes / heuristics:
- If you see cache.evictions_per_min > 1000 concurrent with host cpu/mem spikes, that tends to precede tail latency spikes.
- Prefer rollback to previous routing rather than model downgrade if function-calling is broken.

Quick wins (to consider for next deploy):
- Feature-flag a conservative emergency throttle for embedded jobs that auto-trips if cache.hit_rate < 0.7 and hosted-api.p95 > 2x baseline.
- Add a short-lived export metric for "ephemeral-prefix churn" — count of unique keys inserted in 5m window for each namespace.

End-of-shift summary (04:45 handoff call): service recovered; root cause suspected combination of eval backfills + LRU eviction behavior; created three follow-up tickets (SRE-3124/3125/3126). Next daytime checkpoint: preliminary bucketed eviction sim results and PR for eval-job throttle.

Notes to next oncall: treat this as "probable repeating pattern" if you see small-model routes + embedding backfill running together. If alerted, prioritize cache metrics first.

Raw links referenced: CONFLUENCE-4552 (runbook draft), GITHUB:redwood/serving-runtime#987 (investigation branch), JIRA-SRE-3124/3125/3126 (follow-ups).

-- Ava M. (overnight lead)
